findings.reason: an unmeasurable half of a two-part deliverable lets the node be closed while the diagnosis that the fix is premised on is absent.
findings.text: the done-when requires the report to name why the 08:54Z request was never admitted, but nothing in the gate can fail when it does not, so the node closes on the overtaking assertion alone

findings.reason: the second half of the deliverable should be conditioned on the named cause, since for one listed cause the change is inert and can starve the session §12 exists to keep dispatching.
findings.text: the deliverable makes the queue-behind change unconditional, but for the section's own candidate cause "the admit service's lane filter excluding the pointer (§24's fault class)" the queued request can never be admitted, so queueing same-session dispatches behind it stops the session launching while the request still waits

findings.reason: if the twenty launches came from a different session or lane identifier than the queued pointer's, a same-session check would not have stopped them and the fix would not address the reported starvation; the plan must settle which before specifying the check.
findings.text: the section states "Dispatch and the admission pass already read a session's room through one function, `_dispatch_lane_allowance`, and hold on the same predicate", yet its own evidence has the same session launching twenty-plus same-lane runs in the window when that predicate held its queued request at 0

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_dispatch_lane_allowance` resolves (`reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1268`), the cited review run's commit resolves (`9abe3b66c`), and §24/§3 resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the single negative control falsifies only the overtaking assertion; the first deliverable's outcome ("names the cause found in the first step") has no test, no control and no failing state.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the report and the gate log are placed under the run directory, which is durable, and the test is a new file under `tests/`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach the new symbol or the test filename, and the section text states the mechanism rather than a changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the section asserts both that dispatch and the admit pass hold on the same allowance predicate and that more than twenty same-session, same-lane dispatches launched at once while the queued request's allowance read 0; those two cannot both hold for the same session and lane, and the plan builds an unconditional fix on the unresolved version.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the node's goal is one property, that a session's new dispatch does not overtake its own queued request; the diagnosis that precedes it is a prerequisite step, as in §16, §17 and §24.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §25 declares no `data-links`, and its only real predecessors (§18, §20, §24) have landed, so no shared-file ordering is owed; it writes `queue_admission.py` and `dispatch.py`, which no other still-open section claims.
